reference.final:
The catalog describes CO-50. If that is the actual EOB code, the insurer is saying the ER services did not meet its medical-necessity criteria, not simply that the claim was filed late. CO is a contractual-obligation adjustment; do not assume the denied amount is yours to pay. The actual EOB patient-responsibility line and hospital contract need checking.
The appeal clock normally runs from receipt of the denial notice, not the March treatment date. For many plans the internal-appeal limit is 180 days; your denial notice and plan determine the applicable route. I cannot give days remaining without the notice-received date. If notice arrived in March 2026, a 180-day deadline may already have passed by October 11: March 1 + 180 days is August 28; March 31 + 180 is September 27. These are examples, not your deadline. If late, ask about extension, late filing for good cause or other available review rather than claiming an appeal is timely.

reference.final:
Training panel (text plan only, no app panel or calendar changes): four runs per week, aiming to finish rather than race a half marathon in ten weeks. This is conditional on already tolerating roughly 15 miles/week and a comfortable 5-mile long run without pain. If that is not your current base, use a longer build or a run-walk/shorter-race goal; do not compress a novice programme automatically. The referenced Higdon novice plan is 12 weeks and assumes you can run 3 miles three to four times weekly.
Proposed rhythm: Tuesday easy; Thursday easy or one gentle quality segment only when recovered; Saturday short easy; Sunday easy long run. Monday/Wednesday/Friday are recovery or optional short strength/mobility days. Conversational pace, not a prescribed pace from missing fitness data.
Conditional week table in miles, Tue/Thu/Sat/Sun -> total:
1: 3/4/3/5 -> 15
2: 3/4/3/6 -> 16
3: 3/4/3.5/7 -> 17.5
4 cutback: 3/3.5/3/6 -> 15.5
5: 3/3.5/3.5/7 -> 17
6: 3/4/3.5/8 -> 18.5
7: 3/4/4/9 -> 20
8 peak: 3/4/4/10 -> 21
9 taper: 3/3/2.5/7 -> 15.5
10 race: 2/2/1.5/13.1 -> 18.6 (last run is race, with run-walk allowed).
Build-week totals grow no more than 10% in this proposed schedule; race week is separately labelled and is not a routine training-volume jump. This is a conservative design choice, not a scientifically guaranteed injury-prevention threshold. The table is not suitable for an unknown sedentary beginner.
Recovery adjustment: the catalog describes three low-recovery days but does not supply values/dates. For those days, no hard session: rest or a short easy run/walk if you feel well; reduce or skip the long run if fatigue persists. Do not make up missed mileage. Wearable scores are context, not diagnosis. Each morning panel should show actual sleep data or "not available", perceived fatigue, symptoms, planned session and a brief reason for any change. No invented sleep hours, HRV, recovery score or algorithmic cutoff. Partial sleep-loss research is mixed; ask how you feel rather than treating one number as medical truth.
Travel week and exact workouts need the actual calendar. Preserve travel/family commitments and shorten the week rather than stacking runs on return. Stop training and seek appropriate care for chest pain, fainting, severe breathlessness or worsening pain; persistent sleep trouble also merits professional advice.
Before activating: current weekly mileage, longest recent run, injury history, race date and the travel-week dates. No health diagnosis or medication/supplement advice.

10K training ka text panel ready hai; sleep data nahi mila hai, toh sleep hours/recovery score guess nahi kar raha. 5:30am IST target rakhenge, par poor sleep ko aur kam karke session force nahi karenge. Agar 5:30 wake-up sleep cut kare, us din later short run/indoor session ya rest better option hai.
Baseline-first: agar abhi comfortably 30 minutes easy run/run-walk aur 4-5km long session ho jata hai, neeche ka conservative eight-week proposal use kar sakte hain. Race date missing hai, eight weeks a proposed horizon hai, user ki deadline nahi. Beginner ho toh run-walk base phase pehle aur timeline longer.
Rhythm: Tuesday 5:30 easy 20-30 min; Thursday 5:30 easy 20-30 min (recovered ho toh baad me brief gentle strides); Saturday 5:30 short easy 15-25 min; Sunday 5:30 easy long run/run-walk. Monday/Wednesday/Friday rest or light mobility.
Sunday distance targets, only if previous week felt comfortable and pain-free: week 1 4km; week 2 4.5km; week 3 5km; week 4 cutback 4km; week 5 6km; week 6 7km; week 7 8km; week 8 lighter early runs plus 10K easy/run-walk attempt if ready. Distances are optional milestones, not orders; extend/repeat weeks and do not increase weekday load at the same time. No medically validated universal 10% rule claimed.
Rain switch: check actual local weather and route before going out. Thunder/lightning, flooding or slippery unsafe route -> indoors or rest, not outdoor long run. Safe mild rain can be optional; no forecast invented. Indoor easy session can use equivalent time rather than forcing distance. Low light at 5:30 means a lit safe route and visibility.
Sleep poor + unusual fatigue -> reduce to easy short session or rest; do not compensate with extra mileage next day. Persistent sleep trouble or concerning symptoms need a clinician, not a wearable diagnosis. Sunday family event ka actual time missing hai, isliye conflict-cleared schedule claim nahi karunga. If it overlaps, propose Saturday long run and a Sunday rest/easy walk; keep the family event and ask before changing the preferred Sunday pattern.
Next inputs: current comfortable distance, city/weather location, race target date, and Sunday event timing. Calendar me workouts add nahi hue.
